belongs_to: Figure it Out Q2: 'Construct the following figure.' (the letters S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z, A-H)

Outer tips, clockwise from the top-left: S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z (tip S top-left, T top-right, U right-upper, V right-lower, W bottom-right, X bottom-left, Y left-lower, Z left-upper). Inner (notch) vertices, clockwise from the top: A (top centre), B (right of T, below it), C (right, centre), D (right of W, above it), E (bottom centre), F (left of X, above it), G (left, centre), H (left of S, below it); each is labelled near its vertex. The outline goes S-A-T-B-U-C-V-D-W-E-X-F-Y-G-Z-H and back to S. Outline edges: vertical segments T-B, D-W, X-F and H-S; horizontal segments B-U, V-D, Y-F and Z-H; slanting segments S-A, A-T, U-C, C-V, W-E, E-X, Y-G and G-Z. Straight lines join O to all 16 outline vertices (to the 8 tips and the 8 notches), giving 16 triangles around O: the grey triangles are OAT, OBU, OCV, ODW, OEX, OFY, OGZ and OHS; the white triangles are OTB, OUC, OVD, OWE, OXF, OYG, OZH and OSA. So 8 grey and 8 white.

unclear: Whether the side arcs are exact semicircles on AB and CD is read from the picture, not stated.

belongs_to: A Pointed Arch: 'How do we construct this shape? What supporting lines will you use to draw this arch?'
description: A pointed arch outline in black with its supporting lines in light blue. The arch is symmetric about a vertical axis: it has a sharp cusp (point) at the top, and each side consists of an outward-bulging arc at the bottom (a quarter-circle-like arc from the bottom end going up and inward) joined smoothly to an inward-curving (concave) arc which rises to the apex, so each side has an S-shaped curve. The two supporting lines are straight blue segments from the apex down to the two bottom end points of the arch (left foot and right foot, both at the same height); each blue segment crosses its black curve about halfway, where the curve changes from convex to concave. The bottom of the arch is open (no base line). No labels, no numbers.
unclear: The curve radii are not stated; the changeover point is read as the midpoint of each blue line from the picture.

belongs_to: Fig. 6.11: 'The supporting lines are just two line segments of equal length. If their midpoints are marked, will you be able to construct a pointed arch?' (and Figure it Out Q1 on the next page: 'Use support lines in Fig. 6.11 to construct a pointed arch')
description: Fig. 6.11. Two straight line segments of equal length meeting at a top apex like an inverted V (a symmetric tent shape), the left one going down to the lower left and the right one going down to the lower right, both ending at the same height. A black dot marks the midpoint of each segment (2 dots, one on each segment). No labels or measures. Caption 'Fig. 6.11' below (not part of the picture).

belongs_to: Regular Hexagons (Try This): 'How do we construct a regular pentagon (5-sided figure) and regular hexagon (6-sided figure)? To begin with, try to construct a pentagon and hexagon with equal sidelengths.' - the pentagon
description: A regular pentagon with one vertex at the top (point-up), thin black outline. Each of its 5 sides carries one short tick mark across its middle (5 ticks, meaning equal sides), and each of its 5 interior angles carries one small arc (5 angle arcs, meaning equal angles). No letters, no measures.

belongs_to: Regular Hexagons (Try This): the regular hexagon drawn beside the pentagon
description: A regular hexagon with one vertex at the top and one at the bottom (pointy-top; the left and right sides are vertical), thin black outline. Each of its 6 sides has one short tick mark across its middle (6 ticks, equal sides) and each of its 6 interior angles has one small arc (6 angle arcs, equal angles). No letters, no measures.

belongs_to: Regular Hexagon and Equilateral Triangles: 'What happens when we join the opposite points of a regular hexagon? ... Will all the triangles in the figure be equilateral triangles?' - Fig. 6.12
description: Fig. 6.12. A regular hexagon with a vertex at the top and one at the bottom (pointy-top). Vertices labelled clockwise from the top: A (top), B (upper right), C (lower right), D (bottom), E (lower left), F (upper left). The three long diagonals AD, BE and CF are drawn; they all meet at the centre, labelled O (just below-right of the centre point). This divides the hexagon into 6 triangles (AOB, BOC, COD, DOE, EOF, FOA). No tick marks, no angle marks, no colour. Caption 'Fig. 6.12' below (not part of the picture).
